gaps.sentence: He has a wide ___ (KNOW) of local history.
He's a regular ___ (CONTRIBUTE) to the magazine.
The minister was ___ (CRITIC) for her handling of the flooding crisis.
gaps.explanation: 'Be criticised for' = be attacked verbally; the verb form is needed in the passive.

gaps.sentence: The trainers were ___ (COMFORT) for long walks.
gaps.explanation: 'Were comfortable' — adjective; note the spelling: -able, not -ible.

gaps.sentence: ___ (FORTUNE), the package had already been delivered.
gaps.explanation: The sentence adverb is 'Fortunately' — luckily for us.

gaps.sentence: The new ___ (GOVERN) takes office in May.
The refugees celebrated their ___ (FREE) at last.

gaps.explanation: 'Her confidence' — the noun; 'confident' is the adjective.
